title: Module Review Quiz: STL Algorithms & Ranges (CPP_233 to CPP_240)

slides.title: STL Algorithms & Ranges Overview
slides.prompt: This Module Quiz covers STL sorting, searching, modifying algorithms, lambda expressions, iterators, and modern C++20 Ranges & Views (CPP_233 to CPP_240).

slides.title: std::sort Algorithm (CPP_233)
slides.prompt: Fill in the header file required to use algorithms like std::sort and std::find.

slides.title: Iterator Range for Sorting (CPP_233)
slides.prompt: Which iterators must be passed to std::sort to sort an entire vector 'v' in ascending order?

slides.title: Linear Search with std::find (CPP_234)
slides.prompt: Fill in the function name used to locate the first occurrence of a value in a container range.

slides.title: Binary Search Requirement (CPP_234)
slides.prompt: What precondition must be met before calling 'std::binary_search' on a sequence?
options: The elements in the sequence must be sorted
The container must be std::vector only
The container must not contain any duplicate values
The container size must be an even number
slides.correctAnswer: The elements in the sequence must be sorted

slides.title: Lambda Expression Introducer (CPP_235)
slides.prompt: Fill in the capture clause bracket pair used to start an anonymous inline Lambda expression in C++.

slides.title: Lambda Capture by Value vs Reference (CPP_235)
slides.prompt: What does '[&]' mean in a C++ lambda capture clause?
options: Capture all outer local variables by reference
Capture all outer local variables by value
Do not capture any external variables
Return a reference type from the lambda
slides.correctAnswer: Capture all outer local variables by reference

slides.title: Transform Algorithm (CPP_236)
slides.prompt: Fill in the algorithm name used to apply a modification function to every element in a range.
slides.codeSnippet: std::___(v.begin(), v.end(), v.begin(), [](int x){ return x * 2; });

slides.title: std::accumulate (CPP_237)
slides.prompt: Which header file contains numerical operations like 'std::accumulate'?

slides.title: Count If Algorithm (CPP_236)
slides.prompt: Fill in the predicate algorithm name used to count elements that satisfy a specific condition.
slides.codeSnippet: int evens = std::___(v.begin(), v.end(), [](int x){ return x % 2 == 0; });

slides.title: Iterator Dereferencing (CPP_238)
slides.prompt: Which operator is used to access the actual object value that an iterator points to?

slides.title: C++20 Ranges Header (CPP_239)
slides.prompt: Fill in the header name introduced in C++20 for composable algorithms without explicitly passing .begin() and .end().

slides.title: C++20 Pipe Operator in Views (CPP_240)
slides.prompt: What does the pipe operator '|' do when using C++20 Ranges and Views?
options: Chains/pipes a range or view into a view adaptor function
Performs a bitwise OR operation on all elements
Splits the container into two equal threads
Removes duplicate values from the range
slides.correctAnswer: Chains/pipes a range or view into a view adaptor function

slides.title: Ranges View Adaptor (CPP_240)
slides.prompt: Fill in the view name used in C++20 to keep only elements matching a condition.
slides.codeSnippet: auto result = nums | std::views::___([](int x){ return x > 10; });

slides.title: Lazy Evaluation in Views (CPP_240)
slides.prompt: What is a key benefit of using C++20 Range Views over standard STL algorithms?
options: Views evaluate lazily on-demand without copying the underlying container data
Views run automatically on parallel GPU threads
Views increase compilation speed by avoiding templates
Views can only be used with primitive data types
slides.correctAnswer: Views evaluate lazily on-demand without copying the underlying container data
